answer: Sybil resistance binds each agent identity to a cryptographically attested enclave measurement, such as Intel SGX MRENCLAVE, with an analogous measurement for AMD SEV. A verifier accepts the identity only after checking remote-attestation evidence and policy, so duplicating its software in virtual machines does not yield equivalent identities; creating new identities requires purchasing distinct physical silicon that can be attested. A ripple of clones therefore fails, unlike the fable of an orchard grown from seeds.
